purpose: Replace local L4/L6 rank and breadth tuning with structurally different prediction and decision mechanisms.

hypotheses.definition: Expanding same-code same-weekday mean open-to-close return, shifted one session and shrunk to the expanding weekday market mean with prior strength 20.
hypotheses.prediction: Persistent stock-specific weekday effects improve ranking beyond generic recent means.

hypotheses.definition: Penalize the shifted maximum stock open-to-close return over the previous 20 observed sessions.
Rank by shifted 60-session stock mean minus one half of downside semideviation.
hypotheses.prediction: Persistent intraday alpha with limited left-tail exposure dominates mean-only ranking.

hypotheses.definition: Estimate TDnet category effects separately for Friday or weekend-aged disclosures with empirical-Bayes shrinkage; compare with a non-event control.
hypotheses.prediction: Lower-attention release timing produces more same-day continuation after the open.

hypotheses.definition: Monthly expanding Ridge on each training date's winsorized, cross-sectionally standardized open-to-close return.
hypotheses.prediction: Daily z-scores retain economically useful magnitude while removing market-level shifts.

hypotheses.definition: Daily-rank Ridge with exponentially decaying date weights and a 60-session half-life.
hypotheses.prediction: Smooth recency weighting adapts better than expanding or hard rolling windows.

hypotheses.definition: Daily-rank Ridge with exponentially decaying date weights and a 120-session half-life.
hypotheses.prediction: A slower decay preserves structural signal while reducing regime staleness.

hypotheses.definition: Fit separate rank models below and above the prior-only market-volatility median and route each score date using its prior market state.
hypotheses.prediction: Predictive relations differ between calm and volatile regimes.

hypotheses.definition: Fit event and non-event ranking experts separately; route rows with point-in-time TDnet availability and use shrinkage when the event expert is sparse.
hypotheses.prediction: Disclosure and non-disclosure rows follow different return-generating processes.

hypotheses.definition: Optimize one softmax list per training date against the within-date return-rank distribution with L2 regularization.
hypotheses.prediction: A listwise loss aligns training with the daily top-candidate decision better than pointwise Ridge.

hypotheses.definition: Optimize one softmax list per training date against clipped positive return after 40bp cost.
hypotheses.prediction: Concentrating probability on net-profitable outcomes improves realized portfolio return.

hypotheses.definition: Predict the conditional 25th percentile of open-to-close return and rank by that lower quantile.
hypotheses.prediction: A downside-aware conditional quantile is more robust than a conditional mean.

hypotheses.definition: Rank by predicted median minus one half of the predicted median-to-25th-percentile downside gap.
hypotheses.prediction: Separating location and downside improves tail-adjusted return.

hypotheses.definition: Train rank models on multiple strictly prior temporal blocks and rank by the median cross-sectional percentile score.
hypotheses.prediction: Signals that survive training-era changes generalize better.

hypotheses.definition: Rank by mean cross-sectional percentile across temporal-block models minus one half of its standard deviation.
hypotheses.prediction: Penalizing time-instability reduces model-selection and tail risk.

hypotheses.definition: Combine preregistered literature signals using exponentially weighted prior realized net40 performance, updating only after each session closes.
hypotheses.prediction: Online expert weighting adapts to nonstationarity without outcome-informed refitting of the candidate library.

hypotheses.definition: Cluster stocks using strictly prior behavior and predict return residual to the contemporaneous score-date peer centroid.
hypotheses.prediction: Peer-relative deviations isolate idiosyncratic continuation from common group moves.

hypotheses.definition: Train on same-day stock return residualized against a beta-scaled market open-to-close return, with beta estimated only from earlier sessions.
hypotheses.prediction: Removing predictable common exposure improves idiosyncratic candidate ranking.

required_outputs.family_control: Each new family must be compared with its own simplest fixed control.
required_outputs.multiplicity: Report a moving-block family-wise lower bound; no unadjusted winner may be promoted.

stopping_rule: After all registered hypotheses and one preregistered falsification generation, stop reuse of this panel unless a new data source or a new forward period is added.
